correctness.rationale: Deductive elementary proof verified line-by-line and by replay. f=(x-1)g identity holds (expansion checked); disc via Bareiss 9x9 Sylvester =1957=19*103 nonzero so affine model smooth (replay prints PASS, independently re-executed VERIFY_OK). gcd(x-1,g)=1 from g(1)=-1 so g=(x-1)q-1. Identities (2)-(4) verified on -10..10 and hold as polynomial identities (re-derived: 4g-A^2=-(x-2)(x-6), B^2-4g=5x^2-6x+5 disc -64>0 always, 4g-A2^2=3x^2+10x-21). For x>=2 both factors positive (explicit/sandwich-implied) so coprime product square forces each square. Cases x=2 (f=9), x=3,4,5 (strict A^2<4g<B^2=(A+1)^2 with A>0 so 4g nonsquare hence g nonsquare), x=6 (g=37^2 but f=6845 strictly 82^2<f<83^2), x>6 (A2^2<4g<A^2=(A2+1)^2 with A2>0, using 3x^2+10x-21>0 for x>=6 and -(x-2)(x-6)<0) are all correct. For x<=-3, g'=xM with M=4x^2+3x-8, M'=8x+3<0, M(-3)=19 so M>0 and g'<0, decreasing with g(-3)=19>0 gives g>0 while x-1<0 so f<0. Remaining x in {-2,-1,0,1} give f=21,6,-1,0 with 16<21<25, 4<6<9, hence only (1,0). Minor implicit steps (g>0 for x>=2, A2>0 for x>6) are immediate from stated inequalities/values. Supporting point_counts.py correctly segregated as non-proof numerics. No claim about non-integral rationals; DRAFT honestly leaves C4(Q) open.
